title: Session cutpoint KV mirroring and delta reuse for cross-request prompt caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a session cutpoint-based KV mirroring mechanism that captures lightweight snapshots (cutpoints) of request prefix state and stores delta-encoded mirrors to enable safe reuse across interleaved requests. Goal is to reduce redundant KV recomputation for high fanout traffic patterns while keeping GPU residency and eviction costs bounded.
technical_design: Approach: when a request reaches a candidate cutpoint (end of a logical input chunk or tokenizer boundary), we record a compact descriptor: (session_id, cutpoint_hash, top_k_active_kv_slots_bitmap, per-layer kv_digest). We maintain an append-only delta mirror store on CPU with (base_snapshot_id -> list of deltas). During continuous batching, the routing layer will check cutpoint descriptors to determine compatible reuse: identical cutpoint_hash implies zero-copy reuse of GPU-resident KV slice; similar cutpoint (Hamming distance under tunable threshold) will attempt delta application on-GPU if the delta size < threshold_bytes. To keep GPU memory stable, we introduce a mirror crediting system (residency_credits) and a background compactor that consolidates frequently-reused mirrors into packed GPU slabs for amortized residency costs.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces token compute for repeated conversational fragments and multi-tenant prompt templates; improves tail latency under high concurrency by avoiding re-warmups.
Cons: added complexity in routing and bookkeeping; potential CPU memory growth for delta store if compaction not aggressive.
Operational: requires metrics for mirror hit/miss, delta size distribution, and residency credits to tune eviction policies.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror store API implemented with snapshot and delta write/read endpoints (CPU-backed).
Routing layer consults cutpoint descriptors and can decide: exact reuse, delta-apply reuse, or full recompute.
End-to-end integration in continuous batching path with feature flag 'cutpoint-mirror-v1'.
Benchmark: 15-30% reduction in average per-token GPU FLOPs for simulated multi-session chat workload (with 60% repeated prefix overlap).
Memory: GPU resident KV usage should not increase by more than 8% in steady-state for toy benchmark (with residency credits enforced).
Feature gated rollout docs and an SDK toggle for customers to opt in/out.
Unit and integration tests covering eviction, crash-recovery, and cross-shard reuse cases.
steps: Design proto: cutpoint descriptor schema and delta encoding format (varint + run-length).
Implement mirror store on CPU with write-ahead log and LRU compaction hook.
Extend routing: attach cutpoint descriptor to batched requests; add reuse decision logic.
GPU agent: delta-apply patch primitive and residency_credit accounting.
Add telemetry: mirror_hit, mirror_delta_size, residency_credits_used, mirror_eviction_rate.
Run microbenchmarks and compare against baseline (no mirror).
Iterate on thresholds and compaction heuristics based on benchmark results.
Doc + runbook + rollout via feature flag.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with runtime, routing, and infra teams. Agreed on cutpoint descriptor fields and initial delta format. Action: Aisha to draft spec.

2026-02-27: Prototype mirror store implemented (cpu-mirror-v0). Stores full snapshots and emits simple deltas. Local perf indicates ~12% token-cost reduction on synthetic repeat workload. Raised compaction questions.
2026-03-03: Routing changes landed behind feature flag. Added descriptor propagation to batching pipeline. First end-to-end smoke tests passed on dev cluster.
2026-03-08: GPU delta-apply primitive reviewed (PR #7023). Review feedback: add bounds checks and better accounting for CUDA memcpy hotspots. Assigned follow-up to Riley Chen.
2026-03-11: Measured delta size distribution from dev traces: median 2.1KB, 95p 78KB. Decision: enable on-GPU delta-apply only for deltas < 24KB; larger deltas fall back to CPU-apply + re-stage.
notes: We must be conservative about on-GPU writes. If delta-apply causes noticeable GC-like stalls, we will change to CPU-apply + async re-stage flow.
Consider integrating a bloom-filter per snapshot to quickly rule out incompatibility for fast-path checks in the routing layer.
Follow-up: evaluate cross-model reuse (same architecture different quantization) as a separate spike after v1 stabilization.
